mk A "**A hold is never re-checked, and the PR closer to merging does not go first.** \`ordersWithin\` (\`src/work-gate/shared-file-orders.ts\`) sorts a repository's PRs by NUMBER, so the older PR always goes ahead of the later one whatever their state, and the order it prints (\"hold behind #N, don't rebase\") is keyed by the overlap, not by whether the overlap still exists. Instance: agent-org#1131 was told to hold behind #1130 on \`src/serve-by-run.test.ts\` at 11:15Z; #1130's rebase dropped that file at 11:25Z; the two share no file, yet #1131 (approved, DIRTY since #1128) still waited, and #1137 behind it. Three changes: (1) the overlap is re-evaluated on every head change of EITHER PR and the sequencing dropped when it is empty; (2) of two overlapping PRs the one approved and green goes first; (3) a PR already DIRTY against main is told to rebase now, since holding never saved it a rebase." "holds.recheck" "src/work-gate/shared-file-orders.ts" "src/work-gate/shared-file-orders-recheck.test.ts" "the sequencing between two PRs is a function of their CURRENT files and state, so a hold whose overlap has gone is dropped and an approved green PR is never made to wait for a red one." "$OCA" "1. The Acceptance passes with a fixture where #1130-shaped PR drops the shared file and the later PR's hold is dropped, and a fixture where the approved green PR goes first although opened later; both fail on the old code.
2. A PR whose \`mergeStateStatus\` is DIRTY against main gets a rebase-now order and not a hold.
3. The three behaviours sit behind \`holds.recheck\`; OFF is today's ordering byte for byte (a test)."
mk B "**A real test failure is classed as infrastructure because the rate-limit pattern is run over the WHOLE log.** \`readCiFailure\` sets \`rateLimitOrRunnerLost\` from \`RATE_LIMIT_OR_RUNNER_LOST.test(log)\` (\`src/ci-failure-class.ts\`), and \`fallbackClass\` returns \`infrastructure\` first when it is true. agent-org#1130's \`suite\` failed in \`wake.test.ts\` (\"THE CONTROL: A REAL TICK OVER A QUIET QUEUE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A BACKLOG\"); the fixtures in that suite print rate-limit and 502 text, the classifier read it as \`infrastructure\` / \`rerun-after-reset\`, the orchestrator was woken instead of worker-agent-org-908, and the same-head rerun failed identically with nobody told. Two changes: (1) classify on the FAILING ASSERTION lines (the \`\\u2716\` / \`not ok\` lines), not on text anywhere in the log; (2) a rerun at the same head that fails the same way goes to the owner with the assertion, and the order key (which includes the head) must not dedupe that second failure away." "ciClass.assertionsOnly" "src/ci-failure-class.ts" "src/ci-failure-class-assertions.test.ts" "a check's class is read from its failing assertions, and a same-head rerun that fails the same way reaches the owner with the assertion." "$OCB" "1. The Acceptance passes with a log whose fixtures print \"rate limit\" and \"502\" inside a passing test while one assertion fails: class \`own-defect\`, route \`owner\`; and a second same-head failure produces a second order to the owner. Both fail on the old code.
2. A log that is truly a lost runner (no failing assertion line) is still \`infrastructure\`.
3. Behind \`ciClass.assertionsOnly\`; OFF is today's classifier (a test)."
mk C "**The worktree prune deletes the worktrees of sessions with an open PR.** \`src/prune-worktrees.ts\` removes a tree that is \"merged, clean, inactive and not held\" and never asks whether a pull request of the session's branch is open: at 10:10Z and 11:07Z 12+ worktrees (908, 909, 911, 743, ...) were removed because they were \"clean and pushed\", and each worker rebuilt on its next wake. An open PR carrying the session's label (or whose head is the tree's branch) is a hold for the prune, read from one listing per run, and a listing that cannot be read holds EVERYTHING (never a clean-by-default)." "prune.holdOpenPr" "src/prune-worktrees.ts" "src/prune-worktrees-open-pr.test.ts" "a worktree whose branch is the head of an open pull request is never removed by the prune." "$OCC" "1. The Acceptance passes with a fixture where a clean, pushed tree has an open PR (kept, reason named) and a fixture where the listing fails (everything kept, say so); both fail on the old code.
2. Behind \`prune.holdOpenPr\`; OFF is today's prune (a test).
3. The removal log line names the open PR when it holds."
mk D "**Nothing reports an APPROVED pull request that stays DIRTY.** agent-org#1137 and #1131 sat approved and DIRTY behind a red PR for over half an hour and no health signal named it; the gate read the overlap but \`org-health\` never reads \`mergeStateStatus\`. Add the reading: an approved PR whose \`mergeStateStatus\` is DIRTY for more than 30 minutes with no rebase in progress (no push on its head and no owner turn in that time) is a health finding, with its age, so the class is caught by the org and not by the chairman. Also count the chairman's other two signals: holds per PR and reruns that failed the same way." "health.approvedDirty" "src/org-health.ts" "src/org-health-approved-dirty.test.ts" "org-health reports an approved PR that has been DIRTY for 30 minutes, with its age, and the finding clears when the PR rebases or merges." "$OCD" "1. The Acceptance passes: a fixture PR approved and DIRTY 31 min is a finding with its age; 29 min is not; a head push inside the window clears it; both ends fail on the old code.
2. The finding is a signal with a name org-health's digest prints, and it is behind \`health.approvedDirty\` (OFF = no finding, a test).
3. Holds per PR and same-way reruns are two further readings in the same test file."
mk E "**A rebuilt worktree can push without a local typecheck.** After the prune removed worker-agent-org-908's tree, the rebuild's symlinked \`node_modules\` could not resolve \`typescript\`, so the local typecheck and the failing tests were skipped and the work went straight to CI (agent-org#1130). A rebuilt worktree must prove its toolchain resolves before the worker is handed it: \`typescript\` and the test runner resolve from the tree, else the tree is repaired (reinstall) or the claim says it is not ready and the worker is not started in it." "worktree.rebuildCheck" "src/wake.ts" "src/wake-worktree-toolchain.test.ts" "a worktree the wake rebuilds is handed to its worker only after \`typescript\` resolves from it." "$OCE" "1. The Acceptance passes with a fixture tree whose \`node_modules\` link resolves nothing: the wake refuses to start the worker in it and names the cause; fails on the old code.
2. Behind \`worktree.rebuildCheck\`; OFF is today's wake (a test).
3. The refusal is a row write the owner can read, not a silent skip."
ls $S/[A-E].md; sed -n 1,40p $S/C.md
